LESSON: EXTENSIVE SIGN READING FICTION AND NON- FICTION MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Extensive Sign Reading Fiction and Non- Fiction Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Extensive Sign Reading Fiction and Non- Fiction Materials, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: where they meet regularly. i) In groups, learners are guided to share reflections on the books read and sign read. Why is it necessary to read many books?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Extensive Sign Reading Fiction and Non- Fiction Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Team work as learners engage in an after school reading club where they meet regularly

• Learning to Learn: Independent Learning as learners sign read selected materials.

Values:
Integrity: Transparency as learners share reflections on the books read and sign read.

Link to other Subjects:

The learners are able to relate the concept of extensive sign reading to their learning in Kiswahili.
